explanation: A well-formed model must name every entity, use clear labels, and show relationships. Missing names, ambiguous labels, and omitted relationships are all well-formedness problems. The other options refer to different concerns such as detail level, fidelity, or physical design.

options.text: The model is not well-formed because it has naming and relationship defects.
The model is too detailed because it includes too many attributes.
The model is high-fidelity because it reflects real business language.
The model is normalized incorrectly because it needs more indexes.

prompt: A reviewer says a draft data model is hard to use because one entity is unnamed, another is labeled with a vague business phrase, and one relationship is missing. What quality problem is the reviewer pointing to?
